messages:
alex: uploaded a perfetto trace + nsys capture from this afternoon's loadtest: gs://redwood-traces/2026-03-17/nsys_combined_1932100042.trace

alex: symptoms = big end-to-end tail (p99) for seq_len=256 requests when we hit a certain batching boundary. p50 looks fine.

sam: saw the alert from perf-alert. numbers?

perf-bot: perf-alert: end-to-end p99 increased from 210ms -> 510ms (+143%) for /v1/generate since deploy 2026-03-17T14:00Z. Trace attached: nsys_combined_1932100042.trace

alex: quick summary from trace: gateway->runtime span shows an extra ~200ms stall inside the runtime right before the first token kernel. Perfetto timeline has a dense cluster of events labeled `kernel_select` and `kv_cache_lookup`.

lena: opened the perfetto slice. there's an interleaved sequence:
```
nt: request-enter -> gateway-serialize -> kv_cache_lookup -> kernel_select -> kernel_swap -> cuda_launch -> kv_copy_back -> token_emit
```

lena: the `kernel_swap` events correspond to switching from our small-batch kernel to the large-batch kernel mid-execution when a late request joins the batch. the swap path does extra memcpy + relayout.

dan: that matches what I saw in the nsys timeline: two distinct kernels with different grid configs fired for the same logical step. kernel A (small) takes ~1.8ms, kernel B (large) takes ~2.1ms, but the swap/memcopy adds ~180ms because of an unexpected fallback path that flushes the KV cache.

sam: do we have the NVTX markers around kv cache ops? can you paste the relevant perfetto slice?

alex: pasted perfetto snippet (from slice view):
```
perfetto_event:kv_cache_lookup START t=0.000s
perfetto_event:kv_cache_miss -> triggers async prefetch t=0.002s
perfetto_event:kernel_select chosen="small_kernel" t=0.003s
perfetto_event:kernel_swap reason="late-batcher" t=0.035s
perfetto_event:kv_cache_copy_back size=1.2MB t=0.220s
```

alex: reproduced locally with this loadtest command:
```
CLIENT_CONCURRENCY=80 ./tools/loadtest --model gpt-j-6b --seq 256 --batching=dynamic --duration=120s --trace=nsys_combined_local.trace
```

lena: needs to be prioritized. guess: our batching heuristic allows a late request to cause kernel hint flip which in turn invalidates a small-path KV pointer and causes a fallback memcpy.

dan: proposal: make kernel selection idempotent per-batch boundary. i.e. once a batch starts, freeze kernel_hint for all queued items until the next scheduling window. simple patch: change scheduler->choose_kernel to consult batch.metadata->locked_kernel if set.

sam: alternative: try pessimistic selection: prefer large-kernel if batch size uncertainty > 10% during the scheduling window. cheaper than falling back.

alex: I ran one experiment forcing kernel_hint=large for the whole run: p99 dropped from 510ms -> 250ms, but avg GPU utilization dropped slightly (from 78% -> 72%). tradeoff looks reasonable for customer SLAs.

lena: KV behavior note: when the kernel swap happens we also observed that KV cache prefetch futures are cancelled and retried, adding another ~30ms of stalls per request due to serialized memcpy. we should avoid cancelling in-flight cache fetches.

dan: action items:
- alex: attach the nsys capture and the perfetto permalink to the bug (done).
- dan: draft scheduler patch to lock kernel per-batch boundary (wip).
- sam: run 3 A/B loadtests with forced large/small/auto and collect p50/p95/p99 + GPU util.
- lena: instrument KV cache NVTX markers to emit "prefetch_cancel" when we cancel — I want to confirm timings.

sam: noted. I'll schedule the experiments for tonight and add regression thresholds to the perf CI.

perf-bot: perf-note: reproducible with --concurrency >= 60 and seq_len >= 224.

alex: last note: adding a short-term mitigator in the gateway: if batch_window close and joining request would flip kernel_hint, hold the request for up to 10ms to preserve kernel choice. this reduced tail in my quick test. not ideal long term but buys time.

lena: nice. i'll add a unit test for the KV prefetch cancellation and update the perfetto tracing to include `kernel_hint` attribute on the kernel_select slice so we can grep it automatically.

dan: merging wip patch to my branch and will open PR. assigning reviewers: @alex @lena.

alex: thanks team — filing bug RN-8721 with the trace links and planned mitigations.

sam: good follow-ups. ping me if you need help with the perf CI thresholds.

perf-bot: link: https://perfetto.google.com/trace/abcd1234 (nsys->perfetto converted view)

alex: closing loop — will re-run loadtest after PR lands and post updated trace in the thread.
